title: Long TBT — Hawkish Fed Structural Hedge
entry: Initiate on any pullback to $27-$28. Scale in 50% at $28, add 25% at $27.50, final 25% at $27 or breakout above $29.50.
stop_loss: $26 daily close — implies 30Y back below 5.0% on two consecutive sessions
targets: $34 — Warsh signals hike at June FOMC, +19%
catalyst: April FOMC minutes revealed 8-4 hawkish split — the most divided FOMC since October 1992. CME FedWatch at 63% year-end hike probability (up from ~50%). April PCE drops May 27 — hot print confirms the hawkish bias. Warsh first FOMC June 16-17 inherits this baseline.
thesis: TBT (2x inverse long-dated Treasury) is the cleanest structural hedge against the dominant macro headwind while you hold AI/semis longs. The Fed's internal hawkish posture is documented (8-4 vote), the year-end hike is priced at 63%, and the next inflation print (May 27 PCE) is binary in the wrong direction. Even if equities continue higher on AI capex, the 30Y has structural pressure above 5.0% — and an equity book full of long-duration growth names (NVDA, SMH, ASML) needs a rates hedge. TBT moves inversely 2x to TLT, so if 30Y goes from 5.09% to 5.25% (16bps), TBT moves ~6-8%. The asymmetry: if rates stay contained (best case for equities), TBT loses maybe 5%; if rates spike on Warsh signaling a hike, TBT can rip 15-25% and offset equity drawdown. Use as portfolio insurance, not a directional speculation.
bull_case: PCE May 27 prints 3.5%+ YoY (April CPI was 3.8%); CME hike odds jump to 75%+; 30Y breaks above 5.20% on the print, 5.30% by Warsh's June 17 press conference. TBT to $32-34 ($30-34 target zone). Bonus tail: Warsh actually signals a hike at the June meeting (vs. just hawkish forward guidance) — 30Y to 5.50%, TBT to $38+.
bear_case: PCE comes in cool at 3.3% YoY; oil stays sub-$100 sustainably; 30Y mean-reverts to 4.85% on two consecutive closes. TBT drops to $25-26, stop triggered. Warsh's first FOMC press conference is dovish ('data-dependent, patient on tightening') — bond rally, TBT to $24, -16% loss.
invalidation: 30Y closes below 4.85% for two consecutive sessions, OR TBT below $26 daily close

outcome.note: TBT is trading at $37.63 (last data May 18, 2026), well above all three targets ($30.50, $32, $34). The 30Y hawkish thesis is confirmed: 8-4 FOMC vote, 63% hike probability, and Iran re-escalation all sustained elevated long-end yields. Return computed from reference current_price ($28.50) to Target 3 ($34.00): +19.3%. Note: TBT's 52-week range is $31.69-$39.70, indicating the $28.50 reference price predates the current rate-spike regime; actual market returns from a valid entry in the $31-32 zone would be approximately +17% to the $37.63 level.
